ei.title: 7번: Why New Cars Worsen Car Sickness
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: About 25 to 30% of people suffer from car sickness. Their symptoms include nausea, sweating, headaches, and vomiting. Unfortunately, some technological advances make car sickness even worse. Electric cars, for example, are smoother and quieter than traditional cars. This has the downside of preventing passengers from getting used to the movement of the vehicle. With traditional cars, we associate acceleration with the sound of the engine getting louder. Electric cars, however, deprive us of this reference point. Another problem is the number of screens inside electric cars. They discourage passengers from looking outside. This makes it harder for them to correctly perceive their position in space, which worsens the symptoms of car sickness. In the future, fully automated vehicles will probably make things even worse. This is because the act of driving is one of the best ways to prevent car sickness.

questions.passage: About 25 to 30% of people [suffer / benefit] from car sickness. Their symptoms include nausea, sweating, headaches, and vomiting. Unfortunately, some technological advances make car sickness even worse. Electric cars, for example, are [smoother / rougher] and quieter than traditional cars. This has the downside of preventing passengers from getting used to the movement of the vehicle. With traditional cars, we associate acceleration with the sound of the engine getting louder. Electric cars, however, deprive us of this reference point. Another problem is the number of screens inside electric cars. They [discourage / encourage] passengers from looking outside. This makes it harder for them to correctly perceive their position in space, which worsens the symptoms of car sickness. In the future, fully automated vehicles will probably make things even worse. This is because the act of driving is one of the best ways to prevent car sickness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) suffer=겪다/고통받다, (B) smoother=더 부드러운, (C) discourage=단념시키다
det.analysis:
❌ ① benefit — smoother — discourage: (A) benefit(이득)은 suffer(고통)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② suffer — rougher — discourage: (B) rougher(더 거친)는 smoother(더 부드러운)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ③ suffer — smoother — discourage: 원문 일치. 고통받고(suffer), 더 부드럽고(smoother), 단념시킨다(discourage)
❌ ④ suffer — smoother — encourage: (C) encourage(격려)는 discourage(단념)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: suffer from = ~로 고통받다 / smoother = 더 부드러운 / discourage ~ from = ~하지 못하게 하다

This has the downside of [preventing / encouraging] passengers from getting used to the movement of the vehicle. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) advances=발전, (B) preventing=방지하는, (C) deprive=빼앗다
det.analysis:
❌ ① retreats — preventing — deprive: (A) retreats(후퇴)는 advances(발전)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ② advances — preventing — deprive: 원문 일치. 기술 발전(advances), 적응 방지(preventing), 기준점 빼앗음(deprive)
❌ ③ advances — encouraging — deprive: (B) encouraging(격려하는)은 preventing(방지하는)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ④ advances — preventing — provide: (C) provide(제공하다)는 deprive(빼앗다)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: technological advances = 기술적 발전 / preventing ~ from = ~을 방지하다 / deprive us of = 우리에게서 ~을 빼앗다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) associate=연관짓다, (B) perceive=인식하다, (C) automated=자동화된
det.analysis:
❌ ① dissociate — perceive — automated: (A) dissociate(분리하다)는 associate(연관짓다)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② associate — ignore — automated: (B) ignore(무시하다)는 perceive(인식하다)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ associate — perceive — manual: (C) manual(수동의)은 automated(자동화된)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ④ associate — perceive — automated: 원문 일치. 연관짓고(associate), 인식하기(perceive) 어려움, 자동화(automated)
det.tip: associate A with B = A를 B와 연관짓다 / perceive = 인식하다 / fully automated = 완전 자동화된

This has the downside of preventing passengers from getting used to the movement of the vehicle. With traditional cars, we associate acceleration with the sound of the engine getting louder. Electric cars, however, ④<u>deprive</u> us of this reference point. Another problem is the number of screens inside electric cars. They discourage passengers from looking outside. This makes it harder for them to correctly perceive their position in space, which worsens the symptoms of car sickness. In the future, fully automated vehicles will probably make things even worse. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① suffer=고통받다(적절), ② worse→better 오류(기술이 멀미를 악화시킨다는 맥락에서 better는 부적절), ③ smoother=더 부드러운(적절), ④ deprive=빼앗다(적절)
det.analysis:
❌ ① suffer: 'people suffer from car sickness' — 멀미로 고통받다. 맥락 적절
✅ ② better: 'technological advances make car sickness even better' — 원문은 worse. better(더 좋은)는 부적절
❌ ③ smoother: 'Electric cars are smoother and quieter' — 더 부드럽다. 맥락 적절
❌ ④ deprive: '전기차가 감각적 판단 기준을 빼앗는다' — 맥락 적절
det.tip: make ~ worse = ~을 악화시키다. better로 바꾸면 의미 반전

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① quieter=더 조용한(적절), ② movement=움직임(적절), ③ screens=화면(적절), ④ prevent→cause 오류(운전이 멀미 예방인데 cause는 반대)
det.analysis:
❌ ① quieter: 전기차가 더 조용하다. 맥락 적절
❌ ② movement: 차량의 움직임. 맥락 적절
❌ ③ screens: 전기차 내부 화면 수. 맥락 적절
✅ ④ cause: 원문은 prevent(예방하다). cause(유발하다)로 바꾸면 의미 반전
det.tip: prevent = 예방하다 ↔ cause = 유발하다

questions.passage: This has the downside of __________ (prevent) passengers from getting used to the movement of the vehicle.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: of + 동명사: prevent → preventing. 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사
det.analysis: 전치사 of 뒤에는 명사/동명사. prevent → preventing(동명사).
det.tip: 전치사(of/by/for/in) + 동명사(-ing). prevent → preventing

questions.passage: This makes it harder for them to __________ (correct) perceive their position in space, which worsens the symptoms of car sickness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 동사 perceive를 수식하는 부사: correct → correctly
det.analysis: 형용사 correct → 부사 correctly. 동사 perceive를 수식하려면 부사가 필요.
det.tip: 형용사 → 부사: correct + -ly = correctly

questions.passage: About 25 to 30% of people suffer from car sickness. Their symptoms include nausea, sweating, headaches, and vomiting. Unfortunately, some technological advances make car sickness even worse. Electric cars, for example, are smoother and quieter than traditional cars. This has the downside of preventing passengers from getting used to the movement of the vehicle. With traditional cars, we associate acceleration with the sound of the engine getting louder. Electric cars, however, deprive us of __________. Another problem is the number of screens inside electric cars. They discourage passengers from looking outside. This makes it harder for them to correctly perceive their position in space, which worsens the symptoms of car sickness. In the future, fully automated vehicles will probably make things even worse. This is because the act of driving is one of the best ways to prevent car sickness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전기차가 우리에게서 빼앗는 것 = 기준점(reference point)
det.analysis:
❌ ① the number of screens: 화면 수는 별도 문제
✅ ② this reference point: 전기차가 가속-소리 연관 기준점을 빼앗음
❌ ③ traditional cars: 전통 차량을 빼앗는다는 것은 부적절
❌ ④ the best ways: 최선의 방법은 마지막 문장 내용
det.tip: this reference point = 가속과 엔진 소리의 연관성

questions.passage: About 25 to 30% of people suffer from car sickness. Their symptoms include nausea, sweating, headaches, and vomiting. Unfortunately, some technological advances make car sickness even worse. Electric cars, for example, are smoother and quieter than traditional cars. This has the downside of preventing passengers from getting used to the movement of the vehicle. With traditional cars, we associate acceleration with the sound of the engine getting louder. Electric cars, however, deprive us of this reference point. Another problem is the number of screens inside electric cars. They discourage passengers from looking outside. This makes it harder for them to correctly perceive their position in space, which worsens the symptoms of car sickness. In the future, fully automated vehicles will probably make things even worse. This is because __________ is one of the best ways to prevent car sickness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 운전 행위가 멀미를 예방하는 최선의 방법 중 하나이다
det.analysis:
❌ ① the number of screens: 화면 수는 문제의 원인이지 예방법 아님
❌ ② the movement of the vehicle: 차량 움직임은 멀미 원인과 관련
❌ ③ the sound of the engine: 엔진 소리는 기준점이지 예방법 아님
✅ ④ the act of driving: 운전 행위가 멀미 예방의 최선. 자동화 차량은 이를 제거
det.tip: the act of driving = 운전 행위. 자율주행 → 운전 사라짐 → 멀미 악화
